deck-11.strengths: Guardrail-clean exec story with a role-specific ask (COO/CIO/practice lead) and an apt 'junior drafter, not the signatory' analogy.
deck-11.weaknesses: Boundary diagram is sparse with unconnected boxes, the portable-workbench mapping is generic, and there is no pilot timeline.

deck-19.strengths: Vivid, accurately mapped analogies (offline maps incl. 'test drive before trip'; restaurant vs home kitchen) and a clear capacity-math chain labeled as an estimate.
deck-19.weaknesses: Tokens/sec chart featuring a coder model is off-altitude for execs, and the near-empty 'built on-device, no cloud calls' slide is an unsupported claim for this brief.

deck-39.strengths: Honest insight titles ('Model Speed Is Not Task Savings', 'Measure the Work, Not the Hype') and a clean on-device boundary flow.
deck-39.weaknesses: Analogies are near-literal (local model = drafting assistant) and repeated card/analogy templates make several slides feel samey.

deck-41.strengths: Good visual variety: two-lane routing diagram, workflow chevrons, chart and pilot timeline.
deck-41.weaknesses: States 'works where Wi-Fi is restricted' and 'faster than anyone reads' without hedging, has redundant lane slides, and the carry-on analogy is loosely mapped.

deck-73.strengths: The sensitivity x repetition 2x2 matrix is a useful way to decide which lane to use.
deck-73.weaknesses: Label titles, an unhedged 'works offline' claim, made-up memory allocations, and a bar chart that mixes consultants, summaries and hours.

deck-82.strengths: Storyline titles turn guardrails into credibility ('Device Speed Is Not Task Success', 'Authorize the pilot, not a rollout') and the boundary diagram is rich.
deck-82.weaknesses: The portable-office analogy is mostly literal, and the coder-model speed chart adds little for exec sponsors.

deck-96.strengths: Two vivid, well-mapped analogies (in-flight downloads; hotel safe plus concierge for hybrid), a clear lane diagram and an estimate-labeled capacity chain.
deck-96.weaknesses: A sparse hero slide, a tokens/sec slide pitched slightly too technical for execs, and back-to-back analogy slides in the same template.

deck-18.strengths: Strong 'Local By Default, Cloud By Policy' architecture with an approval gate, guardrail-aware memory and throughput slides, and the made-on-device proof.
deck-18.weaknesses: Opens on hardware instead of the IP problem, the model-band hub diagram is decorative, and the architecture text is tiny.

deck-20.strengths: Manufacturing-resonant analogies (MoE as a machine shop; hybrid routing as make-or-buy) and a solid codegen/RAG plus router diagram.
deck-20.weaknesses: Titles read mostly as labels, and the deck lacks an opening 'why local / IP risk' framing.

deck-45.strengths: IP-first framing ('Your IP. Your Local AI Stack.') and skeptic-friendly titles ('Concurrency Needs A Separate Test', 'Make Hybrid Routing An Explicit Decision').
deck-45.weaknesses: The routing-boundary diagram has floating nodes with no connectors, and the analogies are standard workshop/librarian templates.

deck-47.strengths: Made-on-device hook up front, a measured dense-vs-MoE explanation, and shop-floor analogies tuned to a manufacturing audience.
deck-47.weaknesses: Two back-to-back MoE slides are redundant, and one bar chart mixes single-stream and aggregate tokens/s.

deck-64.strengths: Covers the required topics (memory, runtimes, MoE, bands, hybrid, made on device).
deck-64.weaknesses: Misleading 'VRAM and RAM are separate' car trunk/cabin analogy, a 'typing words per second' analogy, a chart labeling 28 models as 28 GiB, label titles and a weak 'Ready to test?' ask.

deck-85.strengths: Clever, accurate analogies (memory views as map zoom, 'don't count streets twice'; MoE as a specialist clinic with a triage nurse).
deck-85.weaknesses: The memory bar splits 128 GB into 64 GB visible plus '64 GB headroom', which implies the views partition memory; titles are mostly labels.

deck-98.strengths: Skeptic-calibrated titles ('Aggregate Throughput Is Not Per-User Speed', 'Hybrid Routing Enforces A Data Boundary') and two real architecture diagrams.
deck-98.weaknesses: Analogies are competent but stock (workshop, library), and the size-band hub diagram is decorative.
